chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Dazawayi who said:
I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), asking him about the wine drinker. So he wrote: 'The wine drinker is an Infidel'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a wine drinker according to Imam Al-Hassan (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this correspondence, Imam Al-Hassan al-Rida (peace be upon him) succinctly rules that the drinker of wine is a 'kafir,' a ruling often interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating a state of major disbelief (kufr akbar) due to the habitual neglect of a divine command, rather than a total exit from Islam. This brevity underscores the gravity of *khamr* in Shia jurisprudence, linking the physical act of intoxication to a spiritual severance from God. The ruling serves as a critical bridge between legal penal codes and theological status, emphasizing that habitual consumption constitutes a denial of God's authority.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Muhammad Bin Dazawayi who said,
‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, asking him<sup>asws</sup> about the wine drinker. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘The wine drinker is an Infidel’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ya’qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Dadhawayh who has said the following:
“I once wrote to abu al-Hassan, asking him (the Imam) about drinking intoxicating liquor. He (the Imam) wrote back in answer, ‘A wine drinker is an unbeliever.’”
